newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIA AT ODDS WITH FRENCH MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIA AT ODDS WITH FRENCH MANAGER.

text.p: Nigeria kick off a four-nation soccer tournament in Tunisia on Thursday with doubts surrounding the future of their absent French manager who guided the team to the 1998 World Cup finals.
Local newspapers have reported that manager Phillipe Troussier wants to leave Nigeria because of contract disagreements with the Nigerian Football Association (NFA).
The NFA has made no comment on the reports but were clearly not in harmony with the manager, who was not accompanying the team to Tunisia.
"Troussier has been on holiday in Morocco without permission for over three weeks now and hasn't contacted us on when he will return," said NFA spokesman Austin Mgbolu.
Eleven players left Lagos for Tunis on Tuesday with local coaches Monday Sinclair and James Peters.
They will be joined by overseas-based players for the knockout Maghrebian tournament with Cameroon, Zambia and Tunisia, Mgbolu said.

Troussier was appointed in March on a six month contract and was given the task of getting Nigeria, the reigning Olympic champions, into next year's World Cup finals in France. They have qualified with a game in hand.
